## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(
  here, dplyr, tibble, tidyr, purrr, stringr, limma, limpa, ggplot2, patchwork,
  readxl, writexl
)
here::i_am("05_Mitochondria/02_test_mito/a_script/02_test_mito.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

Two questions, both following Granata et al. 2021 (Nat Commun 12:7056) and Reisman et al. 2024
(Nat Commun 15:7677), applied here to whole muscle rather than isolated mitochondria. How much
mitochondrial protein did each leg gain? And did any part of the mitochondrion change beyond that
overall gain?

`proteins` is the normalised protein matrix from stage 01. `raw` is the same quantification before
cyclic loess, cut to the same rows, because mitochondrial content has to be read from unnormalised
values. `d` holds the design, the contrasts and the baseline contrast's name; `fit` is the
stage 02 protein fit. `protein_map` links proteins to gene symbols and `membership` lists the
MitoCarta sets from `01_build_mito_sets`.

```{r read}
stage <- here("05_Mitochondria", "02_test_mito")
quant <- here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data")
proteins <- readRDS(file.path(quant, "proteins.rds"))
raw <- readRDS(file.path(quant, "quant_runs", "proteins_slope_0.7.rds"))[rownames(proteins), ]
d <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data", "design.rds"))
fit <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "02_Differential", "c_data", "fit.rds"))
protein_map <- read_excel(
  here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx"),
  "protein_gene_map"
)
membership <- read_excel(
  here("05_Mitochondria", "01_build_mito_sets", "c_data", "01_build_mito_sets.xlsx"),
  "membership"
)
dim(raw)
```

## Check the inputs agree

The protein map must list the matrix rows in order, and the raw matrix must become `proteins.rds`
after cyclic loess and nothing else. If either fails, the raw and normalised readouts below would
not describe the same data. The design must list the samples in the matrix's column order, because
the mitochondrial protein enrichment (MPE) fit and fry match them by position.

```{r check}
stopifnot(
  identical(protein_map$protein, rownames(proteins)),
  identical(colnames(raw), colnames(proteins)),
  identical(rownames(d$design), colnames(raw)),
  identical(normalizeBetweenArrays(raw$E, method = "cyclicloess"), proteins$E)
)
contrast_names <- colnames(d$contrasts)
targets <- proteins$targets
```

## Prepare the sets

`coverage` counts, for each set, the genes MitoCarta lists and how many of them we measure.
`sets` turns the measured genes into a named list, one character vector per set.

MitoCarta keeps small pathways because some functions are one or two proteins, so there is no size
floor. The 20% coverage floor is ours, not a published rule: below it the measured part says little
about the pathway. The complexes are the structural-subunit pathways, "CI subunits" to "CV
subunits".

```{r sets}
coverage <- membership |>
  summarise(listed = n(), measured = sum(measured), .by = c(collection, set)) |>
  mutate(coverage = measured / listed)
sets <- with(filter(membership, measured), split(gene, set))
complexes <- paste(c("CI", "CII", "CIII", "CIV", "CV"), "subunits")
pathways <- sets[filter(coverage, collection == "MitoPathways", coverage >= 0.2)$set]
c(mitopathways = sum(coverage$collection == "MitoPathways"), tested = length(pathways))
```

## Mitochondrial protein enrichment

Mitochondrial protein enrichment (MPE) is the share that MitoCarta proteins take of the summed
protein values, one number per biopsy. The values are the dpcQuant protein estimates before
normalisation, with `2^raw$E` undoing the log2. dpcQuant places each protein at its typical
precursor intensity, so each protein counts once, however many precursors it has. Every protein
group counts toward the denominator. MPE is computed before normalisation because cyclic loess
assumes the typical protein holds still.

```{r mpe}
intensity <- 2^raw$E
is_mito <- protein_map$gene %in% sets$MitoCarta
mpe <- tibble(
  sample_id = colnames(raw), participant = targets$participant, leg = targets$leg,
  treatment = targets$treatment, timepoint = targets$timepoint,
  mpe = colSums(intensity[is_mito, ]) / colSums(intensity)
)
mpe |>
  summarise(mean_mpe_pct = round(100 * mean(mpe), 1), .by = c(treatment, timepoint))
```

log2 MPE goes through the same design and contrasts as the protein fit, as a single outcome row.
With one row there is nothing for `eBayes()` to borrow from, so the test is the plain least-squares
t: estimate over standard error, with `df.residual` degrees of freedom and a 95% interval.

```{r mpe-test}
mpe_fit <- contrasts.fit(lmFit(rbind(log2_mpe = log2(mpe$mpe)), d$design), d$contrasts)
mpe_test <- tibble(
  contrast = contrast_names, log2FC = mpe_fit$coefficients[1, ],
  se = mpe_fit$stdev.unscaled[1, ] * mpe_fit$sigma, df = mpe_fit$df.residual
) |>
  mutate(
    t = log2FC / se, p = 2 * pt(-abs(t), df),
    conf.low = log2FC - qt(0.975, df) * se, conf.high = log2FC + qt(0.975, df) * se
  )
mutate(mpe_test, across(where(is.double), function(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

## Citrate synthase

Citrate synthase activity is the literature's usual marker of mitochondrial content. This is its
protein, read from the stage 02 fit for comparison only. `topTable()` with `sort.by = "none"` keeps
protein order so the row can be picked by name.

```{r citrate-synthase}
cs <- protein_map$protein[protein_map$gene %in% "CS" & protein_map$selected]
citrate_synthase <- map(set_names(contrast_names), function(cn) {
  topTable(fit, coef = cn, number = Inf, sort.by = "none")[cs, c("logFC", "P.Value", "adj.P.Val")]
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "contrast")
as_tibble(citrate_synthase)
```

## Mitochondrial normalisation

Mitochondrial normalisation, as both papers did it: take the mitochondrial proteins out of the
unnormalised data, normalise that subset alone, and refit. Each protein is then read against total
mitochondrial content, so a protein that only rose with the rest of the mitochondrion no longer
shows a change. The papers used VSN; we use cyclic loess, as for the main matrix.

The refit follows stage 02: `dpcDE()` reads the standard errors from `dpcQuant()` as precision
weights, `sample.weights = TRUE` adds one quality weight per sample, and `eBayes(robust = TRUE)`
moderates the variances. `plot = FALSE` skips `dpcDE()`'s diagnostic plot.

```{r mito-fit}
mito <- raw[is_mito, ]
mito$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(mito$E, method = "cyclicloess")
mito_fit <- dpcDE(mito, d$design, plot = FALSE, sample.weights = TRUE) |>
  contrasts.fit(d$contrasts) |>
  eBayes(robust = TRUE)
```

One row per protein and contrast, with the gene symbol and label from the protein map. BH
adjustment is within each contrast.

```{r mito-proteins}
mito_proteins <- map(set_names(contrast_names), function(cn) {
  topTable(mito_fit, coef = cn, number = Inf, sort.by = "none") |>
    rownames_to_column("protein") |>
    select(protein, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val)
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "contrast") |>
  left_join(select(protein_map, protein, gene, label, selected), by = "protein")
head(mito_proteins, 3)
```

## Complexes I to V

fry is limma's fast self-contained gene-set test: it asks whether the proteins of a set, taken
together, moved in one direction, and it allows for correlation between them. It reads limpa's
precision weights from `y$weights`. `ids2indices()` turns each set's gene symbols into row
positions, matching only each symbol's representative protein, as in `01_run_fgsea_and_fry`. fry
returns its own BH FDR per contrast.

`fry_sets()` takes a protein matrix, its weights and a list of sets, and returns one row per set
and contrast. It runs on both fits for the complexes and on the normalised fit for MitoPathways.

```{r fry-helper}
representative <- with(protein_map, set_names(if_else(selected, gene, NA), protein))
fry_sets <- function(y, weights, sets) {
  y$weights <- weights
  index <- ids2indices(sets, representative[rownames(y)])
  map(set_names(contrast_names), function(cn) {
    fry(y, index, d$design, d$contrasts[, cn], robust = TRUE, sort = "none") |>
      rownames_to_column("set")
  }) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "contrast")
}
```

On the standard fit fry asks whether a complex changed; on the normalised fit, whether it changed
beyond overall mitochondrial content.

```{r complex-tests}
complex_tests <- bind_rows(
  standard = fry_sets(proteins, fit$EList$weights, sets[complexes]),
  mitochondria_normalised = fry_sets(mito, mito_fit$EList$weights, sets[complexes]),
  .id = "fit"
) |>
  select(fit, contrast, set, NGenes, Direction, PValue, FDR)
head(complex_tests, 5)
```

## MitoPathways

fry is the confirmatory test here, as in `01_run_fgsea_and_fry`. After normalisation the shared
expansion is gone, so fry already reads change relative to the rest of the mitochondrion, and a
competitive test (camera) would ask the same question again.

fgsea ranks proteins by moderated t and scores how far a pathway's members sit toward the top or
bottom of that ranking. The normalised enrichment score (NES) divides that score by the mean score
of random sets of the same size, so pathways of different sizes compare; its sign gives the
direction. The leading edge is the subset of members that drives the score, the proteins ranked
before the running score peaks. fgsea draws the rings on the volcanoes. It shuffles proteins as if
independent, so on correlated sets such as complex I its p runs small: between legs it calls
pathways that fry does not, and those are leads.

```{r fgsea}
ranked <- map(set_names(contrast_names), function(cn) {
  with(filter(mito_proteins, contrast == cn, selected), set_names(t, gene))
})
set.seed(1)
fgsea_raw <- map(ranked, function(stats) fgsea::fgsea(pathways, stats)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "contrast")
```

Both methods in one table, with each pathway's listed size and coverage.

```{r pathway-tests}
pathway_tests <- bind_rows(
  fry = fry_sets(mito, mito_fit$EList$weights, pathways),
  fgsea = transmute(
    fgsea_raw, contrast, set = pathway, NGenes = size,
    Direction = if_else(NES > 0, "Up", "Down"), NES, PValue = pval, FDR = padj,
    leading_edge = map_chr(leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ";")
  ),
  .id = "method"
) |>
  select(method, contrast, set, NGenes, Direction, NES, PValue, FDR, leading_edge) |>
  left_join(select(coverage, set, listed, coverage), by = "set")
```

## Figures

Three A4 pages go to `b_reports/02_test_mito.pdf`. They share a theme and the arm colours.

```{r theme}
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 9))
arm_colours <- c(BFR = "#B2182B", HLRT = "#2166AC")
```

Page 1: MPE by arm and time, with each leg's pair joined.

```{r mpe-page}
mpe_page <- ggplot(mpe, aes(timepoint, 100 * mpe, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = paste(participant, leg)), alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(group = timepoint), width = 0.3, outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = arm_colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "MPE, % of summed dpcQuant protein values",
    title = "Mitochondrial protein enrichment by arm and time"
  )
```

Page 2: a complex by contrast grid for both fits, coloured by signed −log10 fry FDR.

```{r complex-page}
complex_page <- complex_tests |>
  mutate(
    score = if_else(Direction == "Up", 1, -1) * -log10(FDR),
    contrast = factor(contrast, contrast_names), set = factor(set, rev(complexes)),
    fit = factor(
      fit, c("standard", "mitochondria_normalised"),
      c("standard fit", "mitochondria-normalised fit")
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(contrast, set, fill = score)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = signif(FDR, 2)), size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~fit, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", high = "#B2182B", name = "signed -log10 FDR") +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    title = "Complexes I to V, standard and mitochondria-normalised fits"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1), legend.position = "top")
```

Page 3: volcanoes of the normalised proteins with fgsea rings, drawn by `enrichVolcano`. `as_da()`
and `as_enrichment()` put the protein and pathway tables into its format; the leading-edge genes
become protein labels so the ring's ticks find their points. `dedup_terms()` keeps one pathway per
overlapping cluster, and the ring draws the twelve with the lowest adjusted p.

```{r enrichment}
da <- enrichVolcano::as_da(
  select(mito_proteins, protein, gene = label, contrast, logFC, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val),
  species = NULL
)
enrichment <- fgsea_raw |>
  mutate(leadingEdge = map(leadingEdge, function(genes) {
    unname(set_names(protein_map$label, protein_map$gene)[genes])
  })) |>
  enrichVolcano::as_enrichment(enrichment_test = "fgsea", database = "MitoPathways") |>
  enrichVolcano::dedup_terms(pathways)
```

`volcano()` draws one contrast. As in `02_enrich_volcano_fgsea`, the NES key goes horizontal below
the ring. The baseline contrast is not drawn.

```{r volcano-page}
volcano <- function(cn) {
  enrichVolcano::plot_volcano_ring(
    da, enrichment,
    contrast = cn, title = cn,
    label_mode = "top_per_direction", label_size = 2.6, axis_size = 2.6, point_size = 0.9
  ) +
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top")) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.height = unit(2, "mm"),
      legend.key.width = unit(16, "mm")
    )
}
drawn <- setdiff(contrast_names, d$baseline)
volcano_page <- wrap_plots(map(drawn, volcano), ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Mitochondria-normalised proteins")
```

```{r pdf}
pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "02_test_mito.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
walk(list(mpe_page, complex_page, volcano_page), print)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Summary

Proteins at BH FDR < 0.05 after mitochondrial normalisation, per contrast.

```{r summary-proteins}
mito_proteins |>
  summarise(tested = n(), fdr_05 = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05), .by = contrast)
```

Complexes at fry FDR < 0.05 in each fit, and MitoPathways at FDR < 0.05 by method, per contrast.

```{r summary-sets}
complex_tests |>
  summarise(fdr_05 = sum(FDR < 0.05), min_fdr = signif(min(FDR), 2), .by = c(fit, contrast))
pathway_tests |>
  summarise(fdr_05 = sum(FDR < 0.05), .by = c(method, contrast)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = fdr_05)
```

## Save results

`02_test_mito.xlsx` holds one sheet per table. `03_complex_subunits` reads `complex_tests`.

```{r write}
sheets <- list(
  mpe = mpe, mpe_test = mpe_test, citrate_synthase = citrate_synthase,
  complex_tests = complex_tests,
  pathway_tests = pathway_tests, mito_proteins = mito_proteins
)
write_xlsx(sheets, file.path(stage, "c_data", "02_test_mito.xlsx"))
```
